name: Worm Flows
approach: From the Marble Mountain Sno-Park (2,800 ft) trailhead, the route follows the Swift Creek Trail #244 (blue diamond blazes on trees in winter) north into forest. The trail climbs steadily through timber for roughly 2 miles, gaining to about 3,700-3,750 ft, where it breaks out of the trees near Chocolate Falls, a 40-ft seasonal waterfall on Swift Creek. Just above the falls, cross to the west side of Swift Creek — this ford can be tricky and swollen with meltwater in spring or after warm spells, and the crossing point/sign is often buried in winter snowpack, so treat it as a navigation checkpoint rather than a marked trail junction. Above treeline the route enters the open, barren Worm Flows lava/mudflow terrain; wooden route-marking posts guide climbers from about 3,700 ft up to roughly 4,800 ft, after which large posts thin out and occasional cairns (and, in winter, wands placed by parties) mark the line up broad ridges and open slopes. The route follows Worm Flow Ridge past an old seismic monitoring station near 6,200 ft, then continues up snow/scree slopes to merge with the summer Monitor Ridge climbing route at about 7,400 ft. From that junction it's another ~850 ft of climbing on open slopes to the crater rim, then about a quarter mile west along the rim to the true summit (8,363 ft). There is no reliable water past Swift Creek/Chocolate Falls, so carry everything you'll need for the round trip. Above treeline this is committing, exposed terrain: whiteout conditions, wind, and snow-covered cairns/posts make route-finding the main crux, so carry a map/GPS track as backup even though the line is well-established. Open slopes on the upper mountain can be avalanche terrain when wind-loaded — avoid loaded slopes and gully bottoms after new snow or wind events.

beta: Start at Marble Mountain Sno-Park (2,800 ft). Follow Swift Ski Trail #244 north through dense forest to timberline. Cross to the west side of Swift Creek above Chocolate Falls (3,700 ft). Navigate rocky lava flows and mudflows marked by wooden cairn posts up to approximately 4,800 feet. Continue ascending marked route to a seismic station at 6,200 feet. Final snowfield ascent leads to crater rim at 8,363 feet.
overview: Worm Flows is the standard winter and early-spring route on Mount St. Helens, climbed from Marble Mountain Sno-Park (2,800 ft) when the higher Climbers Bivouac/Monitor Ridge trailhead is snowed in. Named for the lobed lava flows the trail parallels, it's a non-technical but sustained snow climb: roughly 12 miles roundtrip with about 5,700 ft of gain to the 8,363 ft crater rim, typically taking 7-10 hours.

waypoints.name: Marble Mountain Sno-Park
waypoints.note: Standard winter/spring trailhead; climbing permit required above 4,800 ft year-round.
waypoints.directions: From I-5 Exit 21 at Woodland, follow SR 503 east about 30 miles to Cougar. Continue east on Lewis River Road, which becomes Forest Road 90, to the Forest Road 83 junction, turn left and drive about 6 miles to the Marble Mountain Sno-Park, where the road is gated in winter and spring. A Washington Sno-Park permit is required December through March, and a Mount St. Helens climbing permit is required above 4,800 ft year-round.

waypoints.name: Mount St. Helens Crater Rim
waypoints.note: Breaks treeline near 3,700 ft at Chocolate Falls, joins the Monitor Ridge route near 7,400 ft, then follows the crater rim west to the true high point.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Swift Creek Trail #244 north through forest about 2 miles to treeline near Chocolate Falls (about 3,700 ft) and cross to the west side of Swift Creek just above the falls. Follow posts, then cairns and wands, up the Worm Flows onto Worm Flow Ridge past the old seismic station near 6,200 ft, join the Monitor Ridge route near 7,400 ft, climb about 850 ft more to the crater rim and walk a quarter mile west along it to the high point.
